subject.title: [Bug]: exec spawn UNKNOWN after gateway restart — child_process pool not rebuilt

question: Should this issue stay open pending live Windows current-main restart/exec proof, or should maintainers close it as not reproducible without logs?
rationale: Source inspection supports neither the reported pool root cause nor a current-main fix, and an automated repair would be speculative without a live Windows trigger.

options.title: Collect Windows proof first
options.body: Keep this open and request a redacted current-main Windows run showing config-triggered restart followed by immediate exec failure before code changes.

options.title: Close as not reproducible
options.body: Close only if maintainers are comfortable treating the current source contradiction and lack of logs as enough to reject the report.

options.title: Sponsor narrow hardening
options.body: Open a maintainer-owned task to retry transient Windows `UNKNOWN` spawn failures even without proving the restart trigger.

recommendation.title: Collect Windows proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this open and request a redacted current-main Windows run showing config-triggered restart followed by immediate exec failure before code changes.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent blame and earlier spawn fallback work make this the strongest available routing signal for the proof-versus-hardening decision.
